titel: AGI is whatever you want it to be

faehigkeiten.grund: Auslieferung wird je Abruf neu zusammengesetzt (megaphone vergibt je Abruf eine request_event_id, megaphone haengt ein timetoken an, Adresse traegt eine session_id, kein ETag und Cache-Control "max-age=0, no-cache, no-store", Abruf laeuft ueber den Werbedienst megaphone.fm) - Byte-Offsets veralten (bei dynamischer Auslieferung sofort, gemessen 19.08.2026) und die Zeitachse verschiebt sich mit (eine Folge war 57 s kuerzer als 3,5 h zuvor), deshalb sind auch Sprungmarken in Sekunden unsicher

einzeiler: OpenAI announces Astra and claims we are in the AGI era
kurzfassung: OpenAI introduced its new Astra model and claimed that the AGI era has officially begun. The hosts discussed the implications of this rollout, potential security concerns regarding hidden reasoning, and Nvidia's acquisition of Hugging Face. Additionally, Joanna Stern joined the show to preview the upcoming Apple event and discuss John Ternus taking over as CEO.
stichpunkte: OpenAI unveiled the Astra model, with executives declaring the start of the AGI era.
Security researchers raised alarms over Astra's opaque chain-of-thought capabilities.
Nvidia confirmed its acquisition of Hugging Face for nearly 13 billion dollars.
The hosts analyzed OpenAI's heavy enterprise push and positioning ahead of an IPO.
Joanna Stern joined to discuss Tim Cook stepping down and John Ternus becoming Apple's new CEO.
Panelists previewed the upcoming Apple event and debated whether a folding iPhone will be shown.
Don Preston and Jen Tuohy reported live from IFA in Berlin, highlighting new smart home and gadget releases.

clips.hook: OpenAI held a press call to apologize in advance
clips.text: The guest explains that OpenAI held a preemptive press conference to address alignment and safeguards before public backlash over recent model incidents could hit them.

clips.hook: The pandemic actually helped Tim Cook change the keynote format
clips.text: The speaker notes that the shift to pre-recorded streamed presentations proved to be a major blessing for the outgoing Apple CEO.

clips.hook: Apple's folding phone rumors and case leaks
clips.text: The hosts discuss how widespread leaks and case manufacturers sending out parts make it nearly impossible to keep a major new hardware launch secret.

clips.hook: A toothbrush equipped with a camera and water jets
clips.text: The correspondent describes an expensive new toothbrush that uses a built-in camera to spot gaps between teeth and floss while brushing.

clips.hook: A smart home touchscreen controller locked under glass
clips.text: The reviewer expresses frustration at finding a desirable smart home controller trapped inside a display case at a trade show booth.

beschreibung:
OpenAI announced its next big model, GPT-6 Astra, and also, by the way, that AGI is here now.
Today on The Vergecast, we've got an all-star panel to break down the news of the week.
First, senior AI reporter Hayden Field joins us to talk about our supposed AGI era and Nvidia's acquisition of Hugging Face. Then, our friend Joanna Stern pops in to talk about new Apple CEO John Ternus, old Apple CEO Tim Cook, and to, most importantly, speculate on the format of next week's Apple keynote.
We wrap things up with a super-special lightning round from the IFA electronics show in Berlin. Senior reviewer Jennifer Pattison Tuohy and editor Dominic Preston each pick out the five most interesting gadgets they saw at the show.
And two more things: Vergecast producer Travis Larchuk pops in to tell his tale of identity theft woe and warn you that he isn't the one DMing you on Twitter to ask you to be on The Vergecast. Plus, Brendan Carr is a dummy.
